what: post_reduce_op docs do not say the reduce helper programs the packer reduce edge mask (keeps only col 0 for ROW / row 0 for COL) for the whole call; a post-op that moves data (transpose_dest) has its result zeroed at pack. The design relied on transpose_dest as a post-op.
suggest: Document the pack mask in the post_reduce_op contract and offer an option (or note llk_pack_reduce_mask_clear + copy_init re-arm) for post-ops that change the valid region.

what: Design says ragged W extent goes to transfer counts and CB capacities stay nominal; with batch = one tile row of a ragged chunk the batch does not divide the nominal capacity and CB pointers (wrap only on exact limit hit) run past the CB -> silent corruption (golden 4096x1024).
suggest: Planner rule: any CB whose push/pop quantum depends on a ragged extent must be sized per core group (or the quantum must divide capacity); state this in blocking-model.md ragged-tail section.

what: For fabric (multi-device) ops, a --dev run leaves Ethernet cores dead so the next mesh open in the same or next session fails; the wrapper does not reset after a non-hang failure. Mandating --dev exclusively makes multi-test fabric runs impossible without manual dirty-flag resets.
suggest: For fabric ops: allow non-dev for multi-test runs, use --dev one test per invocation, and have run_safe_pytest.sh reset the device after a --dev fabric run (or on the ethernet-core timeout signature).
